source_evidence: You will not be able to sell your fund shares whenever you want. You must wait for the next repurchase offer, which could be as long as twelve months away.
answer: An interval fund generally does not let shareholders sell their shares whenever they choose. Instead, it periodically offers to repurchase shares, often every three, six, or twelve months. The fund may also limit how many shares it buys back in each offer, so you might not be able to sell all the shares you request. This means your money may remain invested until a later repurchase opportunity.
